fig10.claim: The DFT formation enthalpies lie inside the registered error band for the ionic orthophosphates and outside it, always on the over-bound side, for the condensed, acid and hydrated phosphates, the aluminium hydroxide and the sink salt, so the phosphate benchmark does not pass as a set.
fig10.caption_key: One row per phase with a like-for-like formation enthalpy, grouped by family (gaps between groups: phosphates, silicates, Al-O-H phases, the sink salt) and ordered by error within a group. Horizontal axis: DFT minus tabulated formation enthalpy per atom. Grey band: the registered error band. Marker: filled circle, inside the band (benchmarked); open square, outside the band; open diamond, no like-for-like experimental phase (the tabulated phase is a glass). The caption states the uniform oxide correction per oxygen as the explanation of the outside rows.

fig11.claim: The pH window of an aluminium oxide film narrows as the allowed dissolved aluminium falls: the amorphous hydroxide that governs the film has its window inside the crystalline boehmite window and none at the lowest level.
fig11.caption_key: Horizontal axis: pH. Top group: the two published statements (grey bars, no stated Al level for the first). Below it one group per dissolved-Al level (tick labels, mM), highest first; within a group the upper bar (black) is amorphous Al(OH)3, the governing film phase, and the lower bar (blue, hatched) is boehmite, the crystalline reference. A bar ends at the computed pH limit; an open circle at the right edge: the window continues beyond the computed pH range; an open square at the left edge: no pH at which the film stays at that level. Computed at 298.15 K with activities equal to concentrations.

fig14.claim: Few quantities can settle a verdict by measurement alone: most flip values lie outside the present prior range or need a width well below it, and the rows without a registered prior have no required precision at all.
fig14.caption_key: One row per quantity, grouped by the verdict link it settles (gaps between groups). (a) The prior range of the quantity, scaled to width one (grey band; log scale for a log-uniform prior), and the flip value with its 5 to 95 percent range where the output gives one. (b) The required width of the measurement as a fraction of the present prior width (bar from zero). (c) Rows with no numerical required width: left, no flip in the physical range or closed by definition; middle, unreachable at the prior; right, gap or not computable. Marker: evidence grade of the present input (circle A, square B, triangle C, inverted triangle D, diamond ignorance prior, cross no grade); open marker and dashed band: gap row, no registered prior.

fig15.claim: The phosphates that pass K2 in the as-prepared slurry (HAp, ACP, beta-TCP) and the carbonate are thermodynamically excluded at the two higher cutoff classes and open at the lowest, while most amorphous framings and the aluminium phosphates are open or undetermined: passing dissolution stability does not settle the cell regime, and it needs a high dose at the lowest acid-adjusted pH.
fig15.caption_key: One row per phase or baseline, grouped top to bottom: R-slurry phases, R-cell phases, silicate comparators, the carbonate polymorphs (gaps between groups). Columns: K2 in the as-prepared (processing) slurry, then K2 in the acid-adjusted slurry state split by pH (tick labels, pH of the slurry); then one pair of columns per registered K1 cutoff class (tick labels, V vs Li+/Li; the lowest is the nominal class), crystalline framing left and amorphous right. Fill and hatching: suitable against dissolution (dots), undetermined (plain), open (single hatching), thermodynamically excluded (cross hatching); a suitable K2 cell whose minimum passing dose is at or above the high-dose value carries vertical lines as well; no fill: not tested in that column. K1 of the carbonate is drawn on the calcite row.

fig17.claim: Dissolution stability and oxidative stability are separate tests: the candidates that pass K2 over the widest pH range sit at K1 upper bounds below the two higher cutoff classes, and the condensed and aluminium phosphates, which have no pH-dependent K2 map, have an upper bound but no lower one.
fig17.caption_key: (a) One row of markers per candidate that has both a K2 map and a K1 upper bound, at its tier-1 upper bound on the oxidation limit (vertical, V vs Li+/Li); horizontal: slurry pH of the K2 cell sets (acid-adjusted state, then the as-prepared slurry); rows ordered by upper bound, rows with equal bounds offset slightly. Marker area: fraction of cells that pass. Filled circle: the lowest passing dose is below 0.01 mol/dm^3; open circle: at or above it. Cross: thermodynamically excluded at that pH; plus: open; dot: undetermined. (b) Candidates without a pH-dependent K2 map: bar from the upper bound downward with no lower end, the lower bound being pending. Grey line and bands: the registered cutoff classes, lowest to highest.

fig4.claim: The model orders the two surfaces of a case as observed where the case's input acts on the template-nucleus contact (crystal-template adhesion, gamma_sn), and mostly fails where it acts on the template-liquid interface (gamma_sl); overall the retrodiction falls short of its registered pass count, and inputs shuffled across cases come close to it.
fig4.caption_key: (a) One row per usable case, grouped by the interface its input acts on (the record's per-case interface): top group gamma_sn (crystal-template adhesion), then the net-energy case, then gamma_sl (Ca2+ binding and surface-energy cases); within a group by identifier (tick labels). Marker: median of the predicted difference Delta = DG*_het(test) - DG*_het(reference) over the Monte Carlo draws, in units of k_B T; bar: its 5 % to 95 % interval. Marker shape and colour give the verdict of the pass criterion: filled circle, correct; filled square, incorrect; open diamond, inconclusive (the interval contains zero; counted as a miss). Vertical line: Delta = 0. Horizontal axis linear within +-1 k_B T and logarithmic beyond. Narrow column: the observed ordering (right-pointing triangle, the test surface has the higher barrier). (b) Permutation null of the number of correct cases: the fraction of permutations giving each count, inputs shuffled within studies (solid outline) and across studies (dashed outline). Vertical line: the observed number correct. The swap check, N, the number correct, the registered pass count and the null's median and 95 % range are stated in the caption through macros.

fig6.claim: A few inputs carry most of the variance of the predicted barrier on the template, and those inputs need the tightest precision from first-principles validation.
fig6.caption_key: (a) Variance share of each input in log10 of f(theta) DG*_hom(Omega_bulk)/k_B T (link nucleate, primary state of R-slurry), ranked from the top. With correlated inputs (dependence method gaussian_copula) the share is the Shapley effect (filled circles); with independent inputs it is the Sobol first-order (filled circles) and total-order (open diamonds) index. Bars: confidence intervals at the record's level. (b) Required width of each input's prior relative to its present width, on a logarithmic scale, in the same order (configs/preprint/precision_method.md): bars, status ok; open circle at 1, already clears; cross at the left axis limit, unreachable at any width. The caption names the threshold nearest to each input.

fig7.claim: CaCO3 resists dissolution in the slurry only where the calcium dose and the dissolved carbonate keep the bulk supersaturated, and in the cell it is oxidised below the charge cutoffs of most cathode classes; the aluminium-oxide phases have no determined oxidation limit.
fig7.caption_key: (a) R-slurry, C5 dissolution test (Omega_bulk >= 1 with the calcite K_sp and the contract speciation) at each design point: total calcium dose Ca_T (horizontal) by total dissolved carbonate C_T at the parameter table's minimum, value and maximum (vertical). Fill and hatching: verdict of the point (in the caption's order: feasible, plain; inconclusive, single hatching; falsified, cross hatching); the two water-activity points give the same verdict everywhere. Black line: Omega_bulk = 1 at the credible boundary P(Omega_bulk >= 1) = 1/2, interpolated in log Ca_T and C_T between the design points. (b) R-cell, potential vs Li+/Li, the sink of the C5 crossover (the caption names it and states that every other sink is undetermined under every scheme). One group of rows per gated phase (tick label), one row per gas-reference scheme: black, the all-experimental route (governing); blue, JANAF-based and vermillion, MP-based DFT schemes (comparators), dashed where corrected by the benchmark error. Left end: reduction limit; right end: oxidation limit; end tick, determined. An open circle at the axis edge: limit undetermined; an open square: no route for that limit (absent). Grey segment after the governing oxidation limit: the margin m_expt, ending at the falsification bound. Thin dashed vertical lines: the cathode classes' charge cutoffs E_cell_max (class values; the caption identifies them left to right). The 4.025 V bound is stated through a macro.
